concurrent_session_hazard_encountered.description: The local aspose.org-workflows clone at d:/onedrive/Documents/GitHub/aspose.org-workflows was far more stale than assumed (hundreds of commits behind origin/main, not 'kept in sync' as an earlier session memory claimed) and had 3 unrelated uncommitted files from another concurrent session (.github/workflows/www.aspose.org.yml, scripts/deploy/deploy_manifest.json, scripts/deploy/scan_state.json).
concurrent_session_hazard_encountered.what_went_wrong_and_was_corrected: An initial commit was built and the local main ref was advanced on top of the STALE parent before the staleness was discovered. Caught before pushing (a plain push attempt was rejected by the remote as non-fast-forward). The local main ref was restored to its exact original value and the file unstaged via `git restore --staged`, fully undoing the premature advance -- the other session's 3 dirty files were never at risk since the premature commit's tree differed from the stale parent by exactly one new file (no shared paths with the 3 dirty files).
concurrent_session_hazard_encountered.correct_approach_used_for_the_real_push: Fetched origin/main's true current tip, built the commit via an isolated temp index rooted at that real tip (never touching the local main ref or the real working index/tree at any point), and pushed that commit's SHA directly to refs/heads/main on the remote. The local clone's main ref, working tree, and index were byte-identical before and after the entire operation, confirmed via git status --porcelain and git rev-parse main at each step.
concurrent_session_hazard_encountered.lesson: The 64-day-old memory claiming this clone was 'kept in sync' was stale and should not have been trusted without a live git fetch first -- corrected in memory after this session.
